description: A single rendered table (Table 1, "Chemical compositions of the investigated steels") with no micrographs, curves or scale bars. The header spans two levels: a first row reading "Element concentration (wt.%)" and a second row naming eight element columns in the order Mn, Al, C, Nb, V, Mo, W, Fe. Ten data rows give the analysed compositions of the investigated Fe-35Mn-xAl-0.1C steels and of their individual phases: 4Al (Mn 33.92, Al 4.13, C 0.094, Nb 0.11, V 0.11, Mo 1.20, W 0.98, Fe Bal.); 6Al, 6Al_γ and 6Al_α; 8Al, 8Al_γ and 8Al_α; 10Al, 10Al_γ and 10Al_α — the γ and α subscripts denoting austenite and ferrite. Mn ranges from 32.44 to 37.39 wt.%, Al from 4.13 to 10.18 wt.%, and C is quoted only for the bulk alloys (0.076-0.253 wt.%) with a dash "-" for every α and for 10Al_γ, indicating carbon is below detection or not determined in the ferrite. Nb stays near 0.08-0.11 and V near 0.09-0.18 in all rows; Mo and W are 0.80-1.54 and 0.81-1.63 respectively. Fe is reported as "Bal." (balance) throughout. The table documents that measured Al contents match the nominal 4, 6, 8 and 10 wt.% levels and that Al partitions into ferrite.

observations.observation: The table reports element concentration in wt.% for eight elements in the order Mn, Al, C, Nb, V, Mo, W, Fe.
Ten rows are listed: 4Al, 6Al, 6Alγ, 6Alα, 8Al, 8Alγ, 8Alα, 10Al, 10Alγ and 10Alα, i.e. bulk alloy compositions plus separate austenite (γ) and ferrite (α) analyses for the 6Al, 8Al and 10Al steels.
Al content increases monotonically across the bulk steels: 4Al = 4.13 wt.%, 6Al = 5.97 wt.%, 8Al = 8.10 wt.%, 10Al = 10.17 wt.%.
Mn is the largest alloying addition in every row, ranging from 32.44 wt.% (6Alα) to 37.39 wt.% (10Alγ).
Carbon is given as a dash "-" for every α (ferrite) row (6Alα, 8Alα, 10Alα) and also for 10Alγ, indicating no value reported.
Among the rows with a C value, the highest carbon content is 0.253 wt.% in 8Alγ, while the bulk steels are 0.076-0.098 wt.% C.
For each composition family where both phases are listed, Al is higher in the α row than in the γ row: 6Alα 6.83 vs 6Alγ 5.88, 8Alα 8.26 vs 8Alγ 7.10, 10Alα 10.18 vs 10Alγ 8.51 wt.%.
Mo lies between 0.80 wt.% (10Alγ) and 1.54 wt.% (6Alα) and W between 0.81 wt.% (10Alγ) and 1.63 wt.% (6Alα).
Nb is nearly constant at 0.08-0.11 wt.% and V at 0.09-0.18 wt.% across all ten rows.
Fe is not given numerically; every row reads "Bal." (balance).
The caption states the table gives the chemical compositions of the investigated steels.

The citing text states that the compositions of the solution-treated samples were examined by wet-chemical analysis, and that the austenite and ferrite phase compositions were investigated using electron probe microanalysis (EPMA), with the carbon content in austenite calculated using the chemical composition lever rule.
The citing text states the four ingots have nominal compositions Fe-35Mn-xAl-1C-0.1Nb-0.1V-1Mo-1W (x = 4, 6, 8, 10 wt%), referred to as 4Al, 6Al, 8Al and 10Al steels.
The citing text reports measured densities of 7.42, 7.18, 6.99 and 6.84 g cm-3 for the four steels, decreasing with increasing Al; these density values do not appear in the table itself.

subfigures.description: Two-level-header composition table: top header "Element concentration (wt.%)", column header Mn, Al, C, Nb, V, Mo, W, Fe; ten rows labelled 4Al, 6Al, 6Alγ, 6Alα, 8Al, 8Alγ, 8Alα, 10Al, 10Alγ, 10Alα. All values numeric except Fe, which reads "Bal.", and C, which reads "-" for every α row and for 10Alγ.
